title: Ignatius: Epistle to Polycarp: Shorter and Longer Versions

verses.text:
Having
obtained good proof that thy mind is fixed in God as upon an immoveable
rock, I loudly glorify [His name] that I have been thought worthy [to
behold] thy blameless face, i.e., to make personal acquaintance with one esteemed so
highly.

If thou lovest the good disciples, no thanks are due to
thee on that account; but rather seek by meekness to subdue the more
troublesome. Every kind of wound is not healed with the same plaster.
Mitigate violent

attacks [of disease] by gentle
applications. Literally,
“paroxysms by embrocations.”

Some refer this to the mysteries of God and others to things yet
future.

chapters.title: Chapter V.—The duties of husbands and wives

verses.text:
Flee evil arts; but all the more
discourse in public regarding them. Some insert μή, and render,
“rather do not even speak of them.”

Some render, “to the honour of the
flesh of the Lord,” as in the longer recension.

Flee evil arts; but all the more
discourse in public regarding them. Speak to my sisters, that they love the
Lord, and be satisfied with their husbands both in the flesh and spirit.
In like manner also, exhort my
brethren, in the name of Jesus Christ, that they love their wives, even
as the Lord the Church. If any one can continue in a state of purity, i.e., in celibacy.

Literally,
“if he be known beyond the bishop.”

chapters.title: Chapter VI.—The duties of the Christian flock

verses.text:
Give ye As this Epistle, though sent to the bishop, was meant to
be read to the people, Ignatius here directly addresses them.

A military reference, simply
implying the idea of faithful effort leading to future reward.

Comp. Ignatius’ Epistle to the

chapters.title: Chapter VII.—Request that Polycarp would send a messenger to Antioch

verses.text:
Chapter VII.—Request that Polycarp
would send a messenger to Antioch.

Seeing that the Church which is at
Antioch in Syria is, as report has informed me, at peace, through your
prayers, I also am the more encouraged, resting without anxiety in
God, Literally,
“in freedom from care of God.”
